newsitem.title: INDIA: India RBI buys dlrs as rupee looks to break 35.75.
newsitem.headline: India RBI buys dlrs as rupee looks to break 35.75.

text.p: Dollar purchases by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) helped stem the rupee's rise in early interbank trade on Tuesday, dealers said.
The rupee opened at 35.76/77 per dollar and was quoted at 35.745 in early trade before RBI purchases brough it down, they said.
"At the moment it (RBI intervention) is slightly sporadic," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "They (RBI) stepped in as the rupee was threatening to decisively break the 35.75 barrier."
"It is not clear what their intentions are," he said.
The dealer said the rupee could slip to 35.80 if RBI dollar purchases were sustained.
"That would reverse the sentiment," he said. "Otherwise, I think the rupee could drop to 35.78 and bounce back as dollar supplies remain good and demand is poor."
In latest deals the dollars was quoted at 35.772/785 rupees.
